products.name: Workday AI
products.note: HR and finance AI; skills-based talent; predictive analytics; sensitive HR data exposure

profile_text.body:
Workday is a publicly traded enterprise software company, founded in 2005 and headquartered in Pleasanton, California, that provides cloud-based applications for human resources, finance, and IT management. The company trades on the stock exchange under the ticker WDAY and reported revenue of $9,552,000,000 for the fiscal year ending January 31, 2026, according to its most recent 10-K filing.

The company describes itself as offering an enterprise AI platform and positions its core product, Workday AI, as a system for HR and finance functions that incorporates skills-based talent management, predictive analytics, and agentic AI capabilities. The site presents an AI agent framework it calls capable of finding, building, acting, and automating across HR, finance, and IT workflows, and references an integration with a product called Sana as part of this offering.

Workday carries notable legal exposure, with nine cases on record across multiple federal district courts in California, Georgia, Colorado, Maryland, and Virginia, including several matters under the name Meckfessel Poletti v. Workday, Inc. and cases styled Williams v. Workday, Inc., Elias v. Workday, Inc., Hill v. Workday, Inc., Noriega v. Workday, Inc., and Doe v. Workday, Inc. The site's held facts flag the Workday AI product for risks related to sensitive HR data exposure, and the company's heaviest recorded legal exposure by jurisdiction is in California, with 181 matters logged there.
